userStories.title: Create the protocol-region affordance registry
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Create the single prompt-affordance registry, nonce-protected marker grammar, and ACP-safe rendering APIs.

**Motivation** — `src/prompts/sections/diff-access.ts` already carries the whole mechanism: a per-process nonce, an `OPEN`/`CLOSE` delimited region whose body IS the ACP text, and `applyDiffAccess` swapping in a native rendering at dispatch.

**Approach** — Delimited regions with a per-process nonce, not placeholder tokens, and not a builder-time protocol branch. The rationale is unchanged from `diff-access.ts`'s header and is inherited wholesale: the builder cannot know the protocol (resolved after the prompt string exists, and a fallback swap can change it again); a placeholder degrades to a prompt with *no* instructions, while a region degrades to the pre-change text; and a prompt is not all trusted text — findings from earlier iterations and embedded diffs are spliced into the same string, so a marker that content could forge would let it capture the genuine region. One nonce and one marker grammar for all kinds, with `kind` inside the marker. A single `PROTOCOL_REGION_MARKER_PREFIX` then makes "no marker survives dispatch" checkable in one place.

**Scope** — In: create and barrel-export `src/prompts/sections/protocol-region.ts`, with the `diff-access` registry entry only. Out: adapter/dispatch work (US-002), run affordance producers (US-003/US-004), and commit persistence (US-005).

**Interface** — Sections call `wrapAffordance(kind, spec, acpBody)`; dispatch calls `applyProtocolRegions(prompt, { protocol, advertisedTools })`; anything that persists a prompt to disk calls `unwrapProtocolRegions(text)`. The native rendering is emitted only when **every** name in `requires` is present in `advertisedTools`; otherwise the ACP body is kept. Every failure path (unknown kind, unparseable spec, foreign nonce, missing tool, unterminated region) yields the text that shipped before this feature existed.
acceptanceCriteria: When importing from the prompt-sections module, then `wrapAffordance` is available and wrapping returns a string containing the supplied ACP body verbatim and unmodified between opening and closing markers.
When `applyProtocolRegions` applies a wrapped body with protocol `acp`, then it returns exactly the ACP body with no marker text and unchanged surrounding prompt characters.

When `applyProtocolRegions` applies `diff-access` with protocol `native` and advertised `Git` and `Read`, then it returns native rendering naming the spec baseline ref and containing no shell command.
When `applyProtocolRegions` applies `diff-access` with protocol `native` and advertised tools omit `Git`, then it returns the ACP body unchanged.
When `applyProtocolRegions` applies `diff-access` with protocol `native` and `advertisedTools` is `undefined`, then it returns native rendering without tool gating.
When a matching region has invalid JSON spec text and native protocol is applied, then it returns that ACP body.
When a matching region has an unregistered affordance kind and native protocol is applied, then it returns that ACP body.
When a marker has another process nonce, then `applyProtocolRegions` leaves it byte-for-byte untouched under both protocols.
When a prompt has an opening marker without a matching close marker, then `applyProtocolRegions` returns the prompt unchanged without removing characters.
When a prompt contains two regions of different kinds, then one `applyProtocolRegions` call substitutes both regions.
Given wrong-nonce forged content before a genuine region, when native protocol is applied, then the result renders the genuine baseline ref and retains text between forged and genuine markers.
When `unwrapProtocolRegions` receives regions, then it returns each ACP body and leaves no substring equal to the exported marker prefix.
When `applyProtocolRegions` is applied twice to the same prompt, then its second result equals its first result.

routing.reasoning: A new shared parser/registry must safely handle nonce-authenticated regions and multiple conservative failure paths.

userStories.title: Gate diff access by advertised tools at every dispatch turn
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Re-express diff access through the helper and substitute regions using coding tools actually advertised on every dispatch turn.

**Motivation** — `native` does not imply `RunCommand` or `GitCommit` exist.

**Approach** — `resolveCodingToolSupport` resolves **before** the substitution call, and the bound `send` closure substitutes each turn prompt it is handed. The hop's returned `prompt` stays the substituted initial prompt. `resolveCodingToolSupport(options)` is hoisted above substitution because it reads only `options` and no session handle.

**Scope** — In: helper-backed diff adapters, required advertised-tool parameter at the agent adapter, both dispatch seams, and follow-up `send` substitution. Out: non-diff registry entries and their producers (US-003–US-005).

**Interface** — `applyDiffAccess(prompt: string, protocol: PromptProtocol, advertisedTools?: readonly string[]): string`, delegating to `applyProtocolRegions`. `undefined` means "tool set unknown — do not gate", preserving today's behaviour for callers that cannot know it. `wrapDiffAccess(spec, shellBody)` keeps its signature and delegates to `wrapAffordance("diff-access", …). `applyDiffAccessForAgentProtocol(agentName: string, prompt: string, advertisedTools: readonly string[]): string` — third parameter **required**, so a future third dispatch site cannot silently ungate.
acceptanceCriteria: When `wrapDiffAccess` is called with its existing two arguments and applied with protocol `acp`, then it yields the ACP body, preserving the diff-access suite’s existing expectations.
When `applyDiffAccess` receives native protocol and advertised tools omit `Git`, then it returns the ACP body.
When `applyDiffAccessForAgentProtocol` is invoked for a native agent with advertised `Git` and `Read`, then it returns native diff rendering.
When `applyDiffAccessForAgentProtocol` is invoked for a native agent with an empty advertised-tool list, then it returns the ACP body.
When `buildHopCallback` dispatches a native agent whose resolved grants advertise `Git` and `Read`, then the agent receives native diff rendering.
When `buildHopCallback` dispatches a native agent with only `Read`, `Glob`, and `Grep`, then the agent receives the shell body.
When `buildHopCallback` dispatches a non-native agent with a region, then the agent receives no exported marker-prefix substring.
When a hop body calls its bound `send` with a region-containing prompt, then the agent receives a substituted prompt with no marker prefix.
When a hop callback returns its initial prompt, then that prompt is substituted and contains no marker prefix.
When the session run hop dispatches native with grants advertising `Git` and `Read`, then it sends native rendering.
When the session run hop dispatches native with grants advertising neither required tool, then it sends the shell body.

routing.reasoning: This modifies a compatibility API plus both live dispatch paths and the multi-turn closure seam.

modifiedFiles.reason: `applyDiffAccess` gains a third `advertisedTools` parameter and delegates to `applyProtocolRegions`; the invariant that replaces the old one is that native rendering additionally requires `Git` and `Read` to be advertised.
`applyDiffAccessForAgentProtocol` takes a required third parameter; every dispatch site passes the advertised names.
coding-tool support resolves before substitution, and the bound `send` closure substitutes each turn prompt it is handed.
coding-tool support resolves before the prompt is substituted.
its calls pin the two-argument `applyDiffAccessForAgentProtocol`; the invariant that replaces it is that the advertised tool list is a required argument.
asserts native rendering from protocol alone; the invariant that replaces it is native rendering only when `Git` and `Read` are advertised.
carries the same protocol-only assumption on the second hop; same replacement invariant.

userStories.title: Render static checks through run affordances
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace the two static-check hedges with `run-check` and `run-test` protocol regions.

**Motivation** — The hedge is spreading.

**Approach** — `run-check` requires `RunCommand` and natively renders `RunCommand {"command": "<label>"}` for a declared check key. `run-test` requires `RunCommand` and natively renders `RunCommand {"command": "<scopedKey>", "values": {"files": "<path>"}}`.

**Scope** — In: configured self-verification checks and acceptance test-rerun lines. Out: isolation/rectifier test blocks (US-004) and commits (US-005).

**Interface** — Sections call `wrapAffordance(kind, spec, acpBody)`; native rendering is emitted only when every required tool is advertised, otherwise ACP body is kept.
acceptanceCriteria: When self-verification has configured `typecheck`, then its output contains no `if that tool is available to you` phrase.
When configured self-verification is applied with `acp`, then it renders the configured typecheck command and no `RunCommand` call.
When configured self-verification is applied with native protocol and advertised `RunCommand`, then it renders a call whose command is declared key `typecheck` and no shell command string.
When configured self-verification is applied with native protocol without `RunCommand`, then it renders the configured shell command string.
When a self-verification command is unconfigured, then it renders the existing unconfigured line and emits no region.
When the acceptance rerun line has a resolved scoped key and native protocol advertises `RunCommand`, then it renders that key and acceptance path in `values.files`.
When the acceptance rerun line has no resolved scoped key, then it renders only the raw command string under both protocols and no `RunCommand` call.
When the acceptance rerun line is built, then it contains no `if that tool is available to you` phrase.

routing.reasoning: Two existing builders are converted to defined registry shapes while retaining their ACP fallback behavior.

modifiedFiles.reason: asserts the hedge wording in the rendered check lines; the invariant that replaces it is that the section renders one region whose body is the shell string.
asserts the hedge wording in the test-rerun line at lines 241 and 316; the invariant that replaces it is that the line renders one region whose body is the shell string.

userStories.title: Render scoped and full-suite test instructions through affordances
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Convert isolation and rectifier shell test instructions to `run-test` affordance regions.

**Motivation** — A prompt section cannot know which transport will receive it, nor which coding tools that transport was actually handed.

**Approach** — `run-test` requires `RunCommand` and natively renders `RunCommand {"command": "<scopedKey>", "values": {"files": "<path>"}}`. Native rendering is emitted only when every required tool is advertised; otherwise ACP body is kept.

**Scope** — In: isolation scoped-test example and rectifier per-file/full-suite command blocks. Out: no-test isolation path; US-003 static checks; US-005 commits.

**Interface** — Sections call `wrapAffordance(kind, spec, acpBody)`; dispatch calls `applyProtocolRegions(prompt, { protocol, advertisedTools })`.
acceptanceCriteria: When configured isolation is applied with `acp`, then it renders exactly the existing shell example including the surrounding full-suite warning sentence.
When configured isolation for a project with a declared scoped key is applied natively with advertised `RunCommand`, then it renders a `RunCommand` call with `values.files` and no shell command.
When isolation has no configured test command, then it renders the existing `scope each run to the files you changed` wording and emits no region.
When the rectifier per-failing-file block is applied natively with advertised `RunCommand`, then it renders one call per failing file with that file in `values.files`.
When the rectifier full-suite block is applied natively with advertised `RunCommand`, then it names declared key `test`.
When the rectifier full-suite block is applied with `acp`, then it names the same command string the verifier replays.
When rectifier blocks are applied natively without advertised `RunCommand`, then they render shell command strings that ship today.

routing.reasoning: The story updates two prompt producers with established command data and ACP regression requirements.

modifiedFiles.reason: a snapshot (closed-world) covering both the `# TEST COMMAND` block and the isolation section's full-suite warning line; the invariant that replaces it is the same prompt text with each command carried inside a region, so the snapshot is re-recorded.
asserts the `# TEST COMMAND` block as literal text; the invariant that replaces it is that the block is a region whose body is that literal text.

userStories.title: Render commits through affordances and persist ACP templates
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Convert role-task commit instructions to `commit` regions and remove regions before generated templates are written to disk.

**Motivation** — an override file named by `prompts.overrides.<role>` replaces the role-task section wholesale, so persisted template text is loaded in a **later process** than the one that wrote it.

**Approach** — `commit` requires `GitCommit` and natively renders `GitCommit {"message": "<msg>"}`. Anything that persists a prompt to disk calls `unwrapProtocolRegions(text)`. A marker written in one process cannot match in a later process, so persisted output contains ACP body rather than a region.

**Scope** — In: all six role-task `git commit -m` instructions and `promptsInitCommand` output. Out: rendering native affordances inside user-authored override templates; US-003/US-004 test affordances.

**Interface** — Sections call `wrapAffordance(kind, spec, acpBody)`; persistence calls `unwrapProtocolRegions(text)`.
acceptanceCriteria: When implementer role-task output is applied with `acp`, then it renders the `git commit -m` instruction exactly as it ships today, including the story commit message.
When implementer role-task output is applied natively with advertised `GitCommit`, then it renders a `GitCommit` call carrying that message and no `git commit` shell string.
When role-task output is applied natively without advertised `GitCommit`, then it renders the `git commit -m` shell string.
When every commit-naming role-task variant is applied with `acp`, then no result contains the marker prefix.
When every commit-naming role-task variant is applied natively with advertised `GitCommit`, then no result contains a `git commit` shell string.
When `promptsInitCommand` writes templates, then each written template is returned unchanged by `applyProtocolRegions` under both protocols because no region survives persistence.
When `promptsInitCommand` writes the implementer template, then its content equals the template header followed by ACP role-task rendering, including the same commit instruction ACP receives.

routing.reasoning: It changes several role-output branches and the CLI persistence boundary while relying on the helper.

outOfScope: rendering a native affordance inside a user-supplied override template — an override is loaded in a later process, whose nonce cannot match, and is treated as literal text by design.

modifiedFiles.reason: asserts the literal `git commit -m` lines; the invariant that replaces it is that each is a region whose body is that line.
asserts a composed prompt carries the literal `git commit -m` instruction; same replacement invariant.
asserts the content written for each template; the invariant that replaces it is that a written template carries the ACP body and no region marker.

analysis: Audit findings: the original draft omitted the US-001 requirement that `wrapAffordance` be importable through the prompt-sections barrel and omitted the new helper test file from expectedFiles. This revision restores both and preserves every stated AC, including ACP byte-parity/unchanged wording and all six failure-table cases. Codebase fit: src/prompts/sections/diff-access.ts:42-184 is the current nonce/region implementation; src/agents/tool-preamble.ts:43-45 is the agent-to-protocol adapter; src/operations/build-hop-callback.ts:296-318 substitutes before resolving coding support and its send closure at :419-450 currently does not substitute follow-up turns; src/runtime/session-run-hop.ts:22-24 has the same ordering problem. `resolveCodingToolSupport` supplies the dispatch-advertised `tools`, therefore tools.map(tool => tool.name), not agent protocol, must drive native affordance gating. Producers are self-verification (src/prompts/sections/self-verification.ts:28-34), acceptance rerun (src/prompts/builders/acceptance-builder.ts:136-166), isolation (src/prompts/sections/isolation.ts:13-18), rectifier (src/prompts/builders/rectifier-builder.ts), and role-task (src/prompts/sections/role-task.ts). prompts-init currently persists raw role-task content at src/cli/prompts-init.ts:81-88. Architecture is a new shared protocol-region module with a per-process nonce, one grammar, registry, wrap/apply/unwrap APIs, conservative parsing, and diff-access compatibility adapters. A known advertised tool set gates native rendering on every required tool; an undefined set intentionally retains legacy protocol-only behavior. Foreign nonce and unterminated regions remain untouched; malformed JSON, unknown kind, and absent tools retain ACP text. Migration order is helper, dispatch/diff adapter, then run-check/run-test, then commit/persistence. Main risks are forged marker capture, marker survival in retry turns, ACP text drift, native calls for tools never advertised, and nonces persisted across processes.
outOfScope: Deleting or renaming `wrapDiffAccess`, `applyDiffAccess`, `DiffAccessSpec` or `DIFF_ACCESS_MARKER_PREFIX`: the diff-access API is retained as a thin adapter over the new helper so its existing suites remain the regression evidence for this change.
Changing any ACP-arm prompt text. Every ACP rendering must stay byte-for-byte what ships today; the ACP byte-parity suite is the gate.
Native renderings for prompt text that names no affordance (framework hints, install-command prose such as `rectifier-builder.ts:460`, review checklists).

User-authored override templates under `.nax/templates/`: a template a user has edited is literal text and receives no native rendering. Only the templates nax itself writes are covered, and only to the extent that they must contain no markers.
Widening `BUILT_IN_EXEC_PATTERNS`, or any change to what the `Exec` argv branch admits.
Adding new coding tools, or changing which ops declare which tools in `src/operations/*.ts`.
Scoped tool grants (`#374`) and the pathspec interaction noted in `diff-access.ts`'s `renderNative` warning.

The third hand-written register, `src/operations/lint-check.ts:156` and `src/operations/typecheck-check.ts:170`, which carry the same hedge inside a `Finding.message`. Findings are persisted to the review-audit artifacts and re-read by a later process, where a per-process nonce cannot match, so a region there would never render natively. Covering them needs a marker whose lifetime outlives the process, which this spec does not design.
Their existing gate stays as-is: those two sites already withhold the `RunCommand` key when the command was auto-detected rather than declared (`typecheck-check.ts:161-170`).
The dead `src/session/session-keeper.ts` dispatch path (no production constructor found); it is not wired into the substitution seam by this spec.
